items.statement: A field that is C1 near every point of a positive closed ball has integrable divergence and integrable polar-sphere flux, with the exact ball-flux identity.
assumptions: \(n\in\mathbb N\), including zero and one; \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\), \(a\in\mathbb R^n\), \(R>0\).
\(F\) is \(C^1\) locally at every point of \(\overline B(a,R)\). No global regularity, support, integrability or flux identity is assumed.

\(\operatorname{div}F\) is the actual matching-coordinate derivative sum. \(\tau\) is the actual unnormalized polar measure on the unit-sphere subtype. Both volume and boundary integrabilities are conclusions.
The exponent uses natural subtraction: \(n-1=\max(n-1,0)\). Here \(S^{n-1}:=\{\zeta\in\mathbb R^n:\|\zeta\|=1\}\); at \(n=0\) this sphere is empty and \(\tau=0\).

items.title: One harmonic extension has zero flux at every internal radius

source.edition: Harmonic Function Theory, second edition; raw PDF SHA2564e64124f7e36993ee784e575a024505f99d484ccf959d2d3864eae9232af8bf1
source.anchor: Closed-set extension convention printed1/PDF9; zero flux Eq1.3 printed4/PDF12; two filled-ball cancellations in Theorem1.4 printed5/PDF13; explicit sealed real radial specialization
source.attribution: Axler, Bourdon and Ramey obtain Eq1.3 from Green identity and use it on two balls in1.4. This item is the explicit real closed-ball, polar-pairing specialization with one retained extension and all positive subradii. It does not assert full complex arbitrary-domain Eq1.3 or identify the polar measure with general geometric surface area.
source.scope: One actual harmonic neighborhood extension, its actual gradient, literal unnormalized polar sphere measure, all0<r<=R.
source.label: HFT zero-flux use: explicit real closed-ball specialization

items.statement: One harmonic extension agreeing with u on the parent closed ball has integrable zero radial gradient flux for every positive subradius, including the parent radius.
assumptions: \(n\ge2\), \(R>0\), \(u:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\); source standing dimension and positive parent radius are retained literally.
There exists an actual function \(v\), harmonic in a neighborhood of every point of \(\overline B(a,R)\), agreeing with \(u\) on the whole closed ball.
The same extension is chosen before all subradii. Derivatives are taken of it. The original total \(u\) may be arbitrary and discontinuous outside the ball. Radial L1 is a conclusion.

formulae.label: One harmonic extension has zero flux at every internal radius
formulae.tex: \exists v:\quad v=u\text{ on }\overline B(a,R),\quad v\text{ harmonic near }\overline B(a,R),\quad\forall\,0<r\le R,\quad\int_{S^{n-1}}\langle\nabla v(a+r\zeta),\zeta\rangle\,d\tau=0.
